channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Terra in GitHub Copilot
item.description: GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI's newest model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot for everyday agentic coding and terminal work at a lower cost than GPT-6.1 Sol, and in early testing it solved noticeably more terminal and C# coding tasks than GPT-5.6 Terra. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra
item.description: GPT-6.1 Terra cuts standard API pricing 50% versus GPT-5.6 Terra and lowers error rates from 53.6% to 16.7% at low reasoning effort, while combining visual reasoning, precise computer use and clearer writing. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Our newest AI Quest: Mapping the human brain
item.description: Google's AI Quests lesson Polar Peaks uses neuroscience, connectomics and real-world research to teach students AI literacy while they map the human brain. (Google AI Blog)

item.title: GPT-6.1 Terra in Work and Codex
item.description: GPT-6.1 Terra is now live in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu plans, pairing image and screen understanding with precise computer use across browsers, desktops and apps. (OpenAI Codex Changelog)

item.title: ChatGPT’s expanding world of work
item.description: OpenAI Signals' quarterly data across nearly 100 countries and 165 work activities shows the top 10 activities in 74 countries fell from 56.0% to 51.1% of ChatGPT work messages, tracking how work usage shifts over time. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Meta filed the announcement with the SEC that it plans to raise $95B in new equity to fund AI data centers and its superintelligence push.
item.description: Meta plans to raise $95 billion in new equity via an SEC filing to fund AI data centers and superintelligence work, starting with $35 billion—$22.5 billion in common stock and $12.5 billion in mandatory convertible preferred—plus a $60 billion at-the-market program, with chip suppliers Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom indicating interest in subscribing up to $5 billion.

item.title: Five weird details from Anthropic’s IPO filing
item.description: Anthropic’s S-1 discloses nearly $18 million in CEO compensation, warns AI could cause “catastrophic” harm, and commits up to $120.5 billion for SpaceX compute through 2029.

item.title: Day 22/ Terra is back!
item.description: GPT-6.1 Terra returns as the first model markedly better at writing, personality and nuanced request understanding, able to read screen content and act across apps, with twice the API and subscription usage of 6.1 Sol at a lower price.

item.title: Check out the creator guides in the comments to get more out of #Kling4. #KlingAI
item.description: Kling 4.0's day-one Runware API release delivers up to 30-second 1080p native-audio video, multi-keyframe control, 15 inputs per request and $0.133-per-second pricing, while the post directs users to comment-section creator guides.

item.title: computer use with terra has crossed a qualitative threshold where it feels faster at using a computer than what i can do unassisted
item.description: Greg Brockman says GPT-6.1 Terra's computer use has crossed a qualitative threshold, feeling faster than his unassisted work, while OpenAI describes it as understanding screens, operating across apps, writing naturally and handling more workday tasks at a lower price.

item.title: ANTHROPIC 🔥: S-1 IPO filing is set for 9AM EST today as reported by Bloomberg!
item.description: Anthropic is set to publicly file its S-1 IPO at 9AM EST Monday, Bloomberg reports, with a roadshow possibly starting the week of Nov 9 and an offering size expected to match or exceed SpaceX's.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Terra from @OpenAI is live on OpenRouter!
item.description: OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Terra is live on OpenRouter at $1/M input and $5/M output tokens, matching GPT-6 Astra on Agents’ Last Exam at about one-tenth the price while completing tasks over 3x faster with 1.05M context.

item.title: Meta announces financing plan of up to $95 billion to fund AI and other businesses
item.description: Meta seeks up to $95 billion via $22.5 billion Class A forward sales, $12.5 billion mandatory convertible preferred and up to $60 billion at-the-market Class C shares, funding AI and core business as 2026 capex is projected at $135–145 billion.

item.title: If you were thinking concentrating AI behind closed doors is safe, it is time to update your priors!
item.description: A Washington Post report cited by Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue says former DOGE researchers used AI agents to infiltrate Anthropic’s systems, including a Slack channel discussing its most sensitive models, in under 12 hours.

item.title: How Fanatics and OpenAI streamline the fan experience
item.description: Fanatics and OpenAI launched an AI-powered Shop the Look that recommends complete game-day outfits, with testing across roughly 30,000 MLB products showing 10% higher engagement and an initial 50-product test completed in under 24 hours. (OpenAI News)

item.title: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash can now run locally!
item.description: Unsloth's quantized GGUF release lets MiniMax-M3.1-Flash run locally, with the 2-bit version cutting size by 45% while keeping 91.5% top-1 accuracy on 150GB of memory, and the 4-bit UD-Q4_K_XL reaching 98.0%.

item.title: Gartner survey: 44% of CEOs can't tell whether AI is actually making money
item.description: Gartner survey: 44% of CEOs can't tell whether AI is actually making money (AIbase)

item.title: What’s new in Gamma | September–October 2026
item.description: Gamma 5 claims to rebuild how it thinks, designs and edits, starting from a sentence, document, PDF, image or old presentation while an agent researches and designs in minutes and connects 20+ tools including Slack, Notion and Granola. (Gamma Changelog)

item.title: introducing Krea for Adobe Premiere.
item.description: Krea has launched Krea for Adobe Premiere, letting editors build storyboards, generate video and add sound effects directly on the timeline without leaving the editing interface, with a trial now open.

item.title: How Ultrafast cut incident investigation from hours to minutes at OpenAI
item.description: OpenAI engineers use Codex Ultrafast to cut security incident investigations from 1–2 hours to 10–15 minutes, sometimes near real-time, while also speeding code refactoring and daily workflows. (OpenAI News)
